segments.narration: Peat cutters found a face so fresh they called police. Denmark, nineteen fifty, in a bog outside Silkeborg.
He had died around four hundred BC. His stubble, his eyelids and the lines around his mouth were all still there.
Bog water does this. Acidic, cold, and with almost no oxygen, it tans skin instead of letting it rot.
His stomach still held his last meal: a porridge of barley, flax and dozens of wild seeds, eaten a day before he died.
And around his neck, a braided leather rope. He was hanged, then laid carefully in the peat with his eyes and mouth closed.
